doc.title: Dave Bailey and John McNeil Interview, 1959-10-25

title: Foster and Dude Lewis, Wesley Dimes and Eddie Morris
summary: Talk about the deceased Lewis brothers, the trumpeter Wesley Dimes shot in Baton Rouge, and Eddie Morris in Bailey's band.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I knew Dude, man. He used to play with Joe Avery and Wilbur Tillman. That's a guy I knew, Dude. Yeah, he's dead. I have a record in my collection of him.
Yeah, and his brother called him Foster Stan. He's dead too. The tribal place. They both buried.
I never knew Foster.
They both buried? Forst Stan.
Where are they buried?
Greenwood Cemetery. Both of them buried there.
Up there on?
Up in Corbin, up there, around the ice.
Green Street, huh?
Yeah, Greenwood Cemetery.
That's where?
That's where my stepdad is buried. And I got a son-in-law buried up there too.
Wesley Dimes is buried up there too, huh?
Wesley Dimes, he's dead?
Wesley Dimes was killed in Baton Rouge. You didn't know that years ago?
Yeah, I didn't know he was dead. Little Trump was playing him. Yeah. He's played on my brother.
Yeah, I saw his grave up there. Yeah, well you were- He was up there?
Yeah.
Yeah? How you got killed? He was killed by a policeman in Baton Rouge.
Yeah?
Shot him. That's what I heard.
Yeah, what's not coming?
Something to do with his wife, I think, or something. I don't know.
Yeah?
Well, you used to work with him in the Liberty Bell, somebody told me.
I don't know if that boy was dead. He'd been dead, eh? Yeah. A policeman shot him in Baton Rouge. Mm-hmm. That's what I heard.
He's been dead for quite a while. I wrote it all down from the grave, you know. All that.
He'd be a nice kid. I know he was a nice little trumpet player, Wesley Dimes. Yeah, I remember him.
I guess Eddie Morris told me about it, you know. He used to be with you, huh, in that band. Yeah.
He's pictures on there. You see his picture on there? When I showed you- did I show you the picture of the band? No. I never showed you the picture of the band.
You got a picture of the Liberty Bell?
No, I mean Eddie Morris when he was playing with us.
Oh yeah, that picture of the Gibson or the Jackson, I don't remember which it was. No, I never showed you the Liberty Bell.
